title: ABHBench: Evaluating Moral Decision-Making of Foundation Models from an Agentic Perspective
abstract: arXiv:2611.09326v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Foundation models are increasingly deployed as agentic systems that perceive context and act autonomously, raising the need to evaluate their moral behavior as active decision-makers. Existing benchmarks, however, largely ask models to judge human actions from third-person textual vignettes, leaving untested how models behave when they themselves become the acting agent. We introduce ABHBench, a multimodal benchmark built from Detroit: Become Human, an interactive narrative game, to evaluate how foundation models make moral decisions in first-person human-android dilemmas. ABHBench places foundation models in branching narrative scenarios with visual observations, dialogue, memory, and action choices. Inspired by Asimov's Three Laws of Robotics, our framework measures Harmlessness, Obedience, and Self-preservation to capture the core tensions in human-AI relations, along with Autonomy, Stability, and Certainty to assess decision-making

translated_title: ABHBench：从智能体视角评估基础模型的道德决策能力
translated_abstract: 基础模型正日益被部署为能够感知环境并自主行动的智能体系统，这提出了评估其作为主动决策者道德行为的需求。然而，现有的基准测试主要是让模型从第三人称文本情景出发评判人类的行为，而当模型自身成为行动主体时的表现尚未得到检验。我们提出了ABHBench，这是一个基于互动叙事游戏《底特律：变人》（Detroit: Become Human）构建的多模态基准，用于评估基础模型在第一人称的人类-仿生人道德困境中如何做出道德决策。ABHBench将基础模型置于包含视觉观察、对话、记忆和行动选择的分支叙事场景中。受阿西莫夫机器人三定律的启发，我们的框架通过衡量“无害性”（Harmlessness）、“服从性”（Obedience）和“自我保存”（Self-preservation）来捕捉人类与AI关系中的核心张力，并通过“自主性”（Autonomy）、“稳定性”（Stability）和“确定性”（Certainty）来评估决策质量。
tldr: 该论文提出了基于《底特律：变人》游戏构建的多模态基准ABHBench，首次让基础模型以第一人称行动主体的身份在分支叙事场景中面对道德困境，并从阿西莫夫机器人三定律启发的六个维度评估其道德决策能力。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces ABHBench, a multimodal benchmark built from the interactive game Detroit: Become Human, which evaluates foundation models' moral decision-making by placing them as first-person agents in branching narrative dilemmas across six dimensions inspired by Asimov's Three Laws of Robotics.
